Chapter 9: Preparing for Engagement and Marriage.
So, you’ve reached that point where things are feeling clearer, and your relationship might be moving toward engagement. It’s such an exciting moment, isn’t it? But, it can also feel a bit serious—because now, you’re not just imagining possibilities, you’re actually starting to build a future together.
Now, getting ready for marriage is about way more than planning the perfect wedding day. It’s really about creating a strong foundation for the rest of your lives. This season is your chance, as a couple, to tackle some important questions—practical ones, emotional ones, even spiritual ones—side by side.
Let’s talk through a few gentle steps that can really help as you get ready:
First, premarital counseling. This is where you sit down together with a mentor, a counselor, or maybe a faith leader, to have guided conversations about things like communication, money, intimacy, and all those family dynamics that can pop up. It’s a safe space to talk things out and learn more about each other.
Next, creating a shared vision. Take time to talk about your hopes and dreams, and what you both expect from marriage. What roles will each of you play? How will you handle responsibilities or spiritual practices, together? Getting these conversations started now can make a big difference down the road.
Then there’s practical planning. Decisions about where to live, how to manage your finances, and other logistics—these need openness and a little flexibility. You don’t have to have it all figured out, but working through these details together builds trust.
And don’t forget about community support. Keep connecting with mentors, family, and friends who care about you both. Their encouragement and accountability can be so valuable as you move forward.
But let’s not miss the joy in all this. Engagement isn’t just a checklist—it’s a public celebration of your love and your decision to move forward together. Invite people into your happiness! Mark this transition with gratitude and hope, and really savor the moment.
In real life, this might mean taking premarital classes, meeting up with a mentor, or even working through a book together. Sometimes, it’s just about having those honest, sometimes tough conversations about your fears, your expectations, and your dreams.
When you prepare for marriage with intention and care, you’re setting yourselves up for a partnership that’s resilient, joyful, and deeply rooted in shared purpose. And isn’t that what we all hope for?
